references.context: Ring theory: subring T of a commutative unital ring S that contains the image of a specified ring homomorphism R→S and inherits addition, multiplication and 1 from S; the subring is not assumed integrally closed.
references.reason: The subring with inherited ring operations is a reusable construction, distinct from the integrality predicate selecting the elements of the closure.
references.matching_note: The image R→S need not be injective; do not describe it simply as R⊆S absent an identified embedding.

references.phrase: all elements integral over image of R
references.disposition: The quantified set comprehends integral elements inside S; the ambient ring S is part of the definition.

references.reason: Monic polynomial and evaluation are reusable algebraic operations; the quantification over all elements of S is the integral-map condition.

references.context: Commutative algebra: square-zero ideal I of a commutative unital ring A, characterized by I²={0} (equivalently ab=0 for all a,b∈I). The square-zero property is strictly stronger than mere nilpotence of an unspecified positive exponent.
references.matching_note: A square-zero ideal has I²=0, independent of the source's quantified lifting or local ring hypotheses; nilpotence with a larger exponent alone is insufficient.

references.context: Commutative algebra: quotient ring A/I of a commutative unital ring A by an ideal I, with elements additive cosets a+I, operations induced from A and canonical surjective unital quotient map A→A/I. This includes prime-ideal quotients, polynomial-ring quotients and ideal-power quotients; a quotient's being a field, local ring or R-algebra requires additional conditions.
references.matching_note: This is the ordinary quotient ring by an ideal. Distinct specific features of this occurrence (prime ideal, polynomial base ring, local ring, square-zero ideal or powers) remain in its mathematical source. It is not a general quotient module or a quotient topology.

references.phrase: unique compatible lifting S→A of S→A/I
references.disposition: Existence and uniqueness of an R-algebra lift over every square-zero quotient is precisely the defining formal-étale lifting condition. Square-zero ideals, quotient algebras and R-algebra maps are already independently classified, so this should not create a recursively defined unique-lift target.
The source quantifies over all such square-zero extensions, not only split or finite ones.
references.phrase: every R-algebra A and ideal I
